title: New Homes Ombudsman complaints triple in one year
summary:
Complaints to the New Homes Ombudsman have increased threefold in the past year, with a higher proportion of cases being decided in favour of homeowners. The service received 1,802 cases in 2024/25, up from 593 the previous year, whilst compensation awarded increased from approximately £67,000 to nearly £215,000.

title: Leasehold campaigners push for £250 ground rent cap
summary:

title: England’s short-term lets register to launch March 2027
summary:
A national register for short-term and holiday lets in England will become fully operational by March 2027, Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has confirmed. The mandatory online register aims to provide local authorities with comprehensive data on the number and location of short-term lets operating within their jurisdictions.

title: MP opposes 5,600-home development on Croydon green belt
summary:
Plans to build 5,600 homes on green belt land in Croydon have drawn opposition from the local Conservative MP, who has launched a petition against the development. Chris Philp, MP for Croydon South, is challenging the London Plan's housing target for an area between Croydon and New Addington.

title: UK housebuilder formations fall to lowest level since 2022
summary:
New housebuilding company formations in Britain have fallen to a four-year low, with 6,815 firms established in the first seven months of 2026. The decline follows the closure of the Help to Buy scheme and sustained high interest rates, while company administrations have risen 21%.

title: UK property market shows resilience six months into conflict
summary:

title: Subsidence claims jump 140% following record summer heat
summary:
UK insurers are reporting a significant increase in subsidence claims following the hottest summer on record, with Hastings Direct recording a near 140% jump in August claims. The average subsidence claim reached a record £20,000 between April and June, with total 2025 payouts hitting £297 million.
